DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 62 s. 2022 JUL 20 2022 HON. ABRAHAM KAHLIL B. MITRA Chairman Games and Amusements Board Legaspi Tower 200 Paseo de Roxas, Makati City Dear Chairman Mitra This has reference to your letter dated 27 June 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: I. Whether an incumbent and re-elected municipal mayor applying for a professional license as professional boxing promoter to promote a professional boxing event in his locality violates the absolute prohibition of Section 90 of the Local Government Code. 2. Whether it is proper to issue a professional license to a local chief executive without first securing an authority to practice from this Department. Per your representation, the Games and Amusement Board (GAB) is mandated by law to regulate and supervise the conduct of all professional sports in the Philippines. As such, you have the power to issue professional licenses or permits for any person, entity or association performing duties connected with professional sports or games. Hence, the queries. We will answer the queries in one discussion since they are interrelated. May it be respectfully informed that this Department has been consistent with our position in the issues raised herein. Section 90 of the Local Government Code of 1991 is specific regarding the practice of profession of all the municipal and city mayors, viz: "SECTION 90. Practice of Profession. — (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicinq their profession or enqaginq in any occu ation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. Xxx" (Emphasis supplied) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

From the foregoing, governors, mayors of cities and municipalities are prohibited from practicing their professions or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. The rationale is that their offices (governor/mayor) is a full-time job. To acquiesce them to practice their profession may result to conflict of interest. They may be allured to allot more time to engage in any occupation than to the discharge of the duties and functions of his office. Constantly, this Department opined that the prohibition is absolute. 1 Moreover, this is also to ensure that Mayors should extend their undivided attention and thus devote their full time only in discharging their duties and functions being the highest official of the Local Government Unit.2 Thus, the municipal mayor is prohibited from engaging in any occupation, including as professional boxing promoter, as this is within the purview of "other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives". Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: NGAN Unders retary for Local Governme OUSLG/MLl/LLLS/LRALLD/lasm 1 DILG opinion No. 07 s. 2020 2 DILG Opinion NO. 10 s. 2018 Page 2 of 2
